title: Upgrade safety policy compiler and rollback risk scorer for Private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade pipelines currently rely on coarse pass/fail gates and manual operator judgment for canaries. This leads to slow rollouts or undetected degradation that triggers emergency rollbacks. Goal: build a telemetry-driven safety policy compiler and a rollback risk scorer that integrate with the private upgrade orchestrator to automate canary gating and provide actionable rollback confidence scores. Scope: compile high-level safety policies into enforceable checks, ingest runtime telemetry and migration traces, compute a per-cohort rollback risk score, and expose decisions to the rollout controller and runbooks. Out of scope: full ML-based predictive rollback model (we will start with a hybrid rule+lightweight classifier and iterate).
acceptance_criteria: Safety policy DSL defined (subset) and documented in Confluence with examples for latency, error-rate, DB-lag, and state-drift checks
Policy compiler produces enforceable checks that the orchestrator can evaluate at canary step boundaries
Rollback risk scorer returns a normalized score [0.0-1.0] with rationale tags (e.g., latency_p95_regression, kv_warm_miss_spike) for each cohort within 30s of metric ingestion
Automated canary evaluator aborts or advances rollout based on combined policy results + risk score according to configurable thresholds

End-to-end integration test that runs a dry-run upgrade in staging and validates at least three failure modes (latency regression, error spike, schema migration error) result in expected gate behavior
Telemetry dashboards and alerting for false-positive/false-negative incidents created and linked in the ticket
implementation_notes: Design: safety policy DSL (YAML) with predicates: metric delta, absolute threshold, anomaly detection window, stateful checks (schema mismatch, migration-id drift)
Compiler: translate DSL into evaluators that subscribe to metric streams (Prometheus/StatsD), trace logs (Jaeger), and migration events from the orchestrator
Scoring: start with weighted rule scoring + lightweight logistic regression trained on historical incidents; keep model explainability via feature tags
Integration points: canary coordinator, cohort scheduler, rollforward/rollback API, audit logs (for private compliance), and console for human override
Preflight: add synthetic dry-run harness (no DB writes) that exercises migrations and collects baseline signals for each tenant cohort
Safety knobs: max-open-cohorts, abort-window (time to wait for stabilization), risk_thresholds per release-channel (LTS vs edge), and operator-ack overrides
Data retention: keep per-upgrade telemetry and decision rationale for 90 days for postmortems; redact PII before storage
Fallback: when telemetry is unavailable, revert to conservative policy (pause rollout) and send urgent PagerDuty notification
Performance: scorer must evaluate and respond within 30s for canary sizes up to 50 cohorts; profiling plan included
Observability: add trace propagation from orchestrator -> policy evaluator, and surface per-check histograms in Console rollout view
